claims.rationale: Independent charter and annal records identify Offa as Mercian king within or at the terminal bound; they do not assign local territory.
claims.statement: The Mercian kingship under Offa existed during the registered interval.

claims.rationale: The annal names the battle place but gives neither parties nor result.
claims.statement: A battle associated with the place-name Rhuddlan is recorded in 796.

claims.rationale: The royal notice is two years outside the interval and does not prove 780–796 local control.
claims.statement: Gwynedd is a candidate named polity near the terminal interval.

claims.rationale: The monument and synthesis are early ninth-century and retrospective, so continuity into 780–796 remains to be demonstrated.
claims.statement: Powys is a candidate named polity in the corridor near the terminal interval.

claims.rationale: Retrospective attribution coexists with segment, chronology and continuity problems; neither establishes political-boundary equivalence.
claims.statement: Recorded Offa’s Dyke remains had an interval-applicable political or traversal role.

claims.rationale: The records support modern locations of surviving or inferred engineering sections only.
claims.statement: Named earthwork sections are recorded at Treuddyn, Brymbo and Chirk.

claims.rationale: The records identify a distinct parallel work while leaving its relation and date unresolved.
claims.statement: Wat’s Dyke is a distinct recorded earthwork that cannot be merged with Offa’s Dyke by default.

claims.rationale: The cited synthesis identifies the route, but its political meaning in 780–796 is not established.
claims.statement: A Dee–Vale of Clwyd route via Bwlch yr Oernant is relevant landscape context.

evidence_gaps.question: Which corridor localities have interval-applicable evidence of Mercian control?
evidence_gaps.stop_condition: Stop after two targeted follow-ups or when the criterion is met.
evidence_gaps.success_criteria: Two independent, locatable research sources support at least two named localities without inferring area from Offa’s title.

evidence_gaps.question: Can Powys be tied to named corridor localities during 780–796 rather than only retrospectively?
evidence_gaps.stop_condition: Stop after two targeted follow-ups or record Powys as unresolved.
evidence_gaps.success_criteria: Two independent interval-applicable locality observations support Powys and address the later Pillar evidence.

evidence_gaps.question: Does evidence connect Gwynedd to named places in the corridor before the 798 notice?
evidence_gaps.stop_condition: Stop after two targeted follow-ups or retain Gwynedd as bracketing context only.
evidence_gaps.success_criteria: Two independent interval-applicable locality observations support Gwynedd or a documented exclusion from the modeled roster.

evidence_gaps.question: Who fought at Rhuddlan in 796, where was the relevant locality, and what territorial consequence is actually supported?
evidence_gaps.stop_condition: Stop after two targeted follow-ups or keep the event display-only.
evidence_gaps.success_criteria: A page-addressable scholarly source resolves at least parties and place identification while separating conjecture from the annal.

evidence_gaps.question: Which specified dyke sections can be dated to the interval, and what role beyond location is supported?
evidence_gaps.stop_condition: Stop after two targeted follow-ups per selected section or keep all sections out of allocation.
evidence_gaps.success_criteria: Section-specific dating and an independent historical-role claim support one preregistered candidate role; otherwise display-only remains binding.

evidence_gaps.question: Can Wat’s Dyke be dated and assigned a role independently of Offa’s Dyke within the target interval?
evidence_gaps.stop_condition: Stop after two targeted follow-ups and preserve uncertainty.
evidence_gaps.success_criteria: A section-specific date and role are supported or the feature is explicitly excluded from interval modeling.

model_decisions.rationale: No dyke geometry is admitted in phase one. If later acquired legally, section geometry defaults to display context and requires a new supported role claim before any allocation use.
The event is not a control point because participants, outcome and territorial consequence are unstated.
The separate engineering work remains context until date and historical role are supported.
The route is post-window context and cannot yet alter traversal costs or entity allocation.
